Bundle SKU

Order Naming Convention: All Plant Talks orders must include PT

A combination sold as one line but packed as several pieces. Upload the day's orders; each is matched against its own shop's combination list.

Today's orders

The day's order export, PDF or spreadsheet. Only the lines that are combinations are kept — what they hold, and how many of each, so packing knows what to put in the box. Each file uploaded is an order of its own under Pending — orders already there are left alone. Which shop an order belongs to is its file name: PT in the name is Plant Talks, anything else is PartyMonkey, and its lines are matched against that shop's list alone.

Bundles to pack

Tap one to pack it. A finished job moves to Completed and is deleted three days later — long enough to check what was packed, short enough not to pile up.

Bundle SKU Settings

The combination lists the day's orders are matched against — one for each shop, because the same name can mean a different box in each.

PartyMonkey

The export from BigSeller — every combination with the sub-SKUs inside it. Uploading adds what is new and updates what it names; combinations not in the file are left alone, so a file of five is five, not a new catalogue. A file belongs to the card it is dropped on, and nothing it says can reach the other shop's list. Delete a combination from the list below when it has really gone.

Plant Talks

Plant Talks' own list, kept apart from PartyMonkey's. An order with PT in its file name is matched against this list and this list's seeds. Anything with seed or seeds in its name counts as Plant Talks whichever card it was uploaded on, so seeds sitting in the PartyMonkey export are still found here. Anything else sold by both shops belongs on both cards. Uploading adds what is new and updates what it names; the rest are left alone.

Pick List Settings

Which lines on the morning's sheet are not picked off a shelf at all.

Hidden SKUs

A line whose SKU contains any of these is hidden by default, left out of the count and the progress bar, and not waited for by Complete List — anything printed to order rather than picked belongs here. The match is anywhere in the name and ignores capitals, so custom catches Custom Gift Tag-Glossy. They are still there under Hidden only and All items.
A list each, because the two shops stock different things. Which one applies to a sheet is its file name: PT in the name is Plant Talks, anything else is PartyMonkey.
Upload takes a spreadsheet (.xlsx, .csv) or a text file, one word to a row — the column headed SKU if there is one, otherwise the first. Words already on that shop's list are left alone, so a longer version of the same file tops it up. Download saves what is there now, in a file that uploads straight back — which is how a list moves from one shop to the other, or gets kept before somebody prunes it.

Words the voice leaves out

Taken out of the SKU name and the shelf before they are read aloud, and left alone everywhere else — the line on screen still says what it says. For packaging noise worth seeing and not worth hearing on every line: 1pc turns Latex-Cobalt-12Inch-(1pc) into “Latex-Cobalt-12Inch”. One list for both shops, since this is about how a name sounds rather than what is stocked.

Words said a different way

A phone reads a name the way its own voice happens to read it, and on some names that is wrong in a way nobody can work around — PT comes out as a word, 1m as “one em”. Write what is on the sheet on the left and how it should sound on the right, spelled however makes the voice say it: PT → pee tee, 2cm → two centimetre. The line on screen is left exactly as it is — this only changes what is heard. One list for both shops.

USERS & ACCESS

Question of the Day!

One question a day, four answers, one tap. Nobody sees who answered what — only the mix.

Written each day it is a bit of fun and the four answers are in no particular order. The hand-written sets below are yours to order how you like; if you use them to track how the team is doing, keep running them most → least, because that is what lets two differently worded days be compared. Keep the names short — they sit under a circle on a phone.

Write it each day
Gemini makes up the question and its four answers, once each morning. Everyone gets the same one.

Leave it empty and it picks its own subject — anything at all, different every day. Put something here and the week’s questions are about that instead. Either way it is meant to be daft and hard to choose between, and never about work.

Written, and coming up

Any day already here is left alone, so setting one ahead is how you decide tomorrow’s rather than leaving it to chance. Editing a day that has been answered changes the wording under the answers already given.

SHIPMENT

China Ship Fee

Domestic delivery inside China for this order, split evenly across every piece on the order.

Split the fee across

“Arrived pcs only” loads the whole fee onto pieces that are already in a box — pending lines carry no China cost until they arrive.

SHIPMENT

Box Size

One shipment can arrive in several boxes. Measure each box, then tick which SKUs were inside it.

Charge freight per

“Its Own Box” charges each box’s freight only to the pieces inside it. “Shared Across All Boxes” pools every box’s freight and spreads it evenly over all ordered pieces, so each piece carries the same average rate.

Print template

Build a sheet from your artwork — card size, layout, cut lines and sheet size, then export a print-ready PDF.

PRINT TEMPLATE

Gift Tag

Pick a design, type the words, set the quantity. The sheet fills itself and starts another page when it runs out of room. Tap a tag to work on that line, then drag its words to move them or the corner to resize the box — that line only. Zoom in fills the view with the tag being worked on; + and − or the wheel take it closer or further out, and dragging the paper between the tags moves the view about. Words too long for their box wrap onto a second line, and shrink from there. Click a text and press space to hold the sheet to it — nothing else can be picked up until space is pressed again.

SHEET
1

Canvas & base layer

▾

The sheet everything prints on, in mm, and the one image printed under every tag. A layout SVG carrying its own size sets the sheet for you.

＋
No file
2

Order

▾

One row per design the customer asked for. Pick the design, type the words, set how many. Tap a word to open how it is set — font, size, align, curve, and a saved phrase to drop in — one word at a time, with rotation, box and outline behind the button inside it. Where the words sit is dragged on the sheet, not keyed here. Text on this line only adds a box to these tags alone, leaving the design as it is for every other line. An outline stands that many millimetres outside the letters, in whatever colour is keyed beside it. Hold a line and drag it to move it up or down the run — the first line fills the first placeholder.

Size of the layout on the sheet

The whole layout is scaled to this and centred. It starts at the file's own size where the file says what that is, and fitted to the sheet where it does not.

Where it sits

The top-left corner of the layout, measured from the top-left of the sheet. It centres itself until you say otherwise.

Or a plain grid

Placeholders on the sheet

Nudge one, resize it, or drop one you do not want. Reset builds them again from the layout file, or from the grid where there is no file.

4

Design Library

▾

Designs, fonts and saved phrases live in a folder on this computer or on the network. Pick it once and the app remembers it; copy the folder to a colleague and she has the whole library. Chrome and Edge on a computer only — elsewhere, use the library file below.

Anything put in the folder is picked up on its own the next time you come back to this window: artwork becomes a design, a font file a font, an SVG the sheet. The subfolders designs, fonts and shape are where the app keeps things tidy, but a file dropped straight into the folder is read just the same. Each is taken on once and never copied — a file already there is used where it lies — and anything you take out of the library stays out.

Designs

Artwork in the designs folder is the library: a new file there becomes a design the next time you come back to this window. It is taken on once, by the name it has, so nothing arrives twice — and one taken out with × stays out until you add it back from the list below.

A one-off design is for artwork a customer sent for this job alone: it is uploaded, printed and forgotten, never written into the folder and gone when the page is reloaded. A picture on the clipboard is the same thing — paste it anywhere on this screen and it lands on the line being worked on. Put the file in the designs folder instead if it should come back.

Share the library

One file holding every design, font and phrase. Send it on; whoever opens it imports once and has the lot. Importing adds what is new and leaves what is already there alone.

GIFT TAG

Design

Drag a text box to move it, or its bottom-right corner to resize; arrow keys nudge it half a millimetre, with Shift two and Alt a tenth. Shift-click picks out several, and Ctrl+G ties those into a group that moves as one (Ctrl+Shift+G unties it). Click a box and press space to hold the tag to it — nothing else answers until space is pressed again. Everything here is the design's default — an order can override the words, the font and its size without touching this.

ONE TAG

The whole tag at its finished size, with the artwork fitted inside it — the guide underneath and the cut shape on top, both as the sheet will place them.

Base layer over the artwork — to line up against a design that covers it. This screen only; the sheet always prints it underneath.

Cutting reference line

▾

Auto-generated from your placeholders — a corner mark at every corner of every card, offset outward, tracing that card's own width and height. Always sits at the very bottom layer, underneath the artwork.

▾

Margin shift

Nudges the reference marks, placeholders and artwork together as one unit, on top of the sheet — set separately per side to correct printer registration drift. Positive X shifts right, positive Y shifts down.
